description: Single-edit mutations of production source, each paired with the test that must detect it and the message that test emits when it does. A mutation that no test rejects is a gap in the proof, not a passing build. `runner: pytest` entries mutate the Python tooling and are proved by its own tests; `profile: release` entries need the engine's debug invariants out of the way so the named test is what observes the defect.

mutations.rationale: A driven port's destructor is host code. Dropping a removed request's waker while the state mutex is held lets that destructor re-enter the governor and deadlock it.
A 1e6 fixed-point scale floors cost*SCALE/weight to zero for large weights, so weighted share silently degrades to arrival order.
Residual deficit carried across busy periods lets an intermittently-active class bank credit and then run its whole backlog ahead of a peer that was queued throughout.
A cancelled request that never ran must not leave virtual-time debt; otherwise a class is punished for work it did not receive.

mutations.rationale: Removing a permit without invalidating the ticket that granted it hands the waiter a permit id with nothing behind it.
mutations.note: Run in release: in a debug build the engine's own structural invariant (`assert_consistent`: every Granted ticket maps to a live permit) fires before the named test can observe anything, which would credit the invariant, not the test. Defence in depth also means a single edit cannot hand the waiter a dead permit id any more — `claim` re-checks the permit and answers Terminal(Released) — so what the test detects is the lost *reason* (Released instead of Reclaimed): the first layer's job.

mutations.rationale: Saturating the running total before comparing it to the budget makes an overdraft compare as 'fits' at the top of the u32 domain.
Behaviour-preserving edit (`x.max(0)` on an unsigned value). The suite must stay GREEN; this proves the runner can report a survivor and is not merely detecting a broken build.
mutations.note: Control mutation: this edit is behaviour-preserving, so the suite must stay GREEN. It proves the runner reports a survivor instead of always finding a failure.

mutations.rationale: Returning memory at a stage boundary is permit activity; a sweep that ignores it reclaims work that was demonstrably alive moments earlier.
Using the raw clock sample instead of the monotonic commit watermark lets a delayed admission stamp a brand-new lease as already stale.
Interpolating a semantic class identifier straight into an OS thread name panics during host setup, outside the worker's own unwind boundary.
An immediate Admitted that arrives after the acquisition budget expired must not start the caller's work.

mutations.rationale: Drawing the whole inter-arrival at the current rate and only then crossing boundaries lets one long off-phase draw skip entire burst phases; the realized rate falls ~200x below the configured stationary rate.
A trace that runs backwards moves virtual time backwards during replay. It must be rejected with the offending index, never silently accepted or re-sorted.
Applying coordinated-omission correction to an open-loop population invents samples; the quantile then describes a synthetic population rather than the requests that were admitted.

mutations.note: The mode assertion precedes the population assertion in the test; either is the intended detection.

mutations.rationale: Rounding the requested iteration count to a multiple of the thread count makes the timed work differ from Criterion's denominator by up to threads-times at small batches.
If the first wake() panic aborts the loop, every later waiter in the same pass is left parked with nobody left to wake it.
mutations.expect_message: every healthy waiter in the same pass was notified

mutations.rationale: Charging the original estimate rather than the remaining reservation resurrects units a stage boundary already returned.
mutations.expect_message: reconcile must not re-reserve returned units

mutations.rationale: Selecting before checking the budget lets the 65th selection debit a DRR deficit / move the ring cursor / advance WFQ virtual time for a dispatch that is not made; the continuation pass then starts one class late.
mutations.expect_message: order must equal the reference across every budget seam

mutations.rationale: Dropping the empty-own-queue condition queues a gap arrival behind its class head unconditionally — including behind a head blocked on another capability pool, pinning the newcomer to that pool's saturation (the head-of-line loss D08's exception exists to prevent).
mutations.expect_message: must not be queued behind a capability-blocked head

mutations.rationale: The naive ring walk credits one quantum per visit, so a head costing K quanta needs K visits under the state mutex. The work oracle counts examined positions; the bound is O(runnable classes), not O(cost/quantum).
mutations.expect_message: the bound is O(runnable classes), not O(cost/quantum)
mutations.note: Costs in the named test are finite (10_000 quanta) so this mutant terminates and is killed by the count, not by a timeout. The u32::MAX shape is covered by the bounded-wait test in the same file.

mutations.rationale: If a claim is not lease activity, a permit can be reclaimed by the sweep in the window where the host has just taken ownership and is dispatching it.
A degrade whose fallback can never dispatch sheds every degraded request as ClassDisabled — a verdict naming the wrong class — instead of being refused at construction.
D09 asymmetry: the fast path unwinds an immediate Admitted after the budget expired, but the queued path started work on a promotion that raced the timeout.
mutations.expect_message: budget spent: the promotion is not started

mutations.rationale: If the builder never reads ExecutorCapabilities, a cpu gate wider than the adapter's declared workers admits more concurrent CPU work than the pool can run.
mutations.expect_message: fewer declared workers than the gate must be refused

mutations.rationale: A deadline on a class that cannot enforce one used to be dropped and the work run to completion with Ok.
mutations.expect_message: a deadline the class cannot enforce must be refused

mutations.rationale: A RunFor budget accepted on the blocking path and then not applied leaves the caller waiting on a job that cannot be aborted.
mutations.expect_message: TM16-002 blocking run budget: the caller was still waiting
mutations.note: The named test bounds its wait explicitly (5s) and releases the held worker on drop, so this mutant is killed by an assertion, not by a hung test binary.

mutations.rationale: Tearing the owned runtime down before sending the deadline reply makes the caller wait for a blocking child the runtime cannot abort.
mutations.expect_message: TM16-024 deadline answer before teardown: the caller was still waiting
mutations.note: Bounded by the test (5s) with release-on-drop of the held child, so the mutant is killed by an assertion rather than surviving as a hang.

mutations.rationale: Same custody rule on the panic path: the runtime must not be torn down (blocking on children) before the caller hears WorkerPanicked.
mutations.expect_message: panic answer before teardown: the caller was still waiting
mutations.note: Bounded by the test (5s) with release-on-drop of the held child.

mutations.rationale: A `mod x_tests;` that is not under #[cfg(test)] ships with the crate; the checker used to skip such files on the strength of their name alone.

The one D08 overtaking exception: a head waiting on a different capability pool must not hold back a same-class newcomer on an unrelated pool, or one saturated pool idles every other pool the class can use.
mutations.expect_message: must not wait for a capability-blocked head

mutations.rationale: D09 queued path, loop branch: the waiter is woken with its promotion already landed and the budget already spent. The biased select prefers the wake, so this is the path a late promotion takes to start work.
mutations.expect_message: a promotion found after the budget is spent must not start

mutations.rationale: Without the pending-continuation rule a queueable newcomer of another class takes capacity in the lock gap between promotion passes, ahead of earlier arrivals that were only waiting for the next pass.
mutations.expect_message: a queueable newcomer must wait for the pending pass

mutations.rationale: A Reject-overflow class whose memory policy is Queue has a queue; routing QueuedBehind through the overflow policy shed the newcomer as CpuSaturated while cpu and memory were both free.
mutations.expect_message: the class has a queue, so the newcomer joins it

mutations.rationale: The declared-workers check must be exact: one worker short of the gate is fewer. Existing tests used 2 vs 4 and could not separate `<` from `+1 <`.
mutations.expect_message: one worker short of the gate is still fewer

mutations.rationale: A blocking job with a stack request runs on a dedicated thread but is still synchronous; sharing the dispatch kind with the async requested-stack path let it accept a CompleteBy deadline it cannot honor.

mutations.rationale: If the pending-continuation flag only ever accumulates, every direct admit after the first budget overflow is queued forever (`QueuedBehind` with nothing to wait for). Only the shuttle gap model observes the post-drain direct admit under concurrency.
mutations.expect_message: no continuation is owed after the drain: direct admit expected

mutations.rationale: A Reject-overflow class has nowhere to wait; queueing it in the gap sheds it as QueueFull for a queue it never had. Only the shuttle overtake model races such a class against the drain.
mutations.expect_message: an unqueueable newcomer is admitted in the gap or shed with CpuSaturated, never queued
